protocol.name: zxr_layer_anchoring_v1
protocol.description:
This protocol assigns layer surfaces a spatial reference frame and a spatial exclusive zone. On a head-mounted display there is no physical output edge; a layer surface's anchor edges and margins are interpreted on the angular rectangle of its assigned frame, and exclusive zones reserve angular bands rather than pixels.
The mapping from layer-shell terms is fixed as follows. Each frame defines an angular rectangle: a horizontal and a vertical angular extent, centred on the frame's forward axis, advertised by the frame_extent event. The layer-shell anchor bitfield selects edges of that rectangle exactly as it selects output edges: a surface anchored to the top edge is placed with its top at the rectangle's top edge; a surface anchored to two opposite edges is stretched between them in angle; a surface anchored to no edge on an axis is centred on that axis. Margins are expressed in surface pixels by layer-shell; the compositor converts them to angle at the surface's presentation distance (angle = 2·atan(px / (2·d·ppm)), where d is the presentation distance in metres and ppm the surface's pixels-per-metre at that distance, derived from the angular size). Keyboard interactivity and layer ordering keep their layer-shell meaning unchanged.
For example: a status bar anchored top | left | right with an angular size of 40 degrees and an exclusive angle of 3 degrees on a head frame with a 90×70 degree rectangle is presented as a band across the top of the view, spanning 40 degrees horizontally, and content in the head frame that respects exclusive zones avoids the top 3 degrees.
The key words "must", "must not", "required", "shall", "shall not", "should", "should not", "recommended", "may", and "optional" in this document are to be interpreted as described in IETF RFC 2119.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is currently in the experimental phase. Backward incompatible changes may be added without bumping the major version of the extension. As such, gating usage on the protocol's presence is discouraged outside Mura itself.

interface.name: zxr_layer_anchoring_v1
interface.description: The entry point for spatial layer anchoring. It advertises the frames the compositor can currently anchor to and creates anchoring extension objects for layer surfaces.

entry.name: already_anchored
entry.summary: the layer surface already has an anchoring object

enum.name: frame
enum.description: The frame a layer surface is positioned in. Head-framed surfaces follow the view. Body-framed surfaces follow the user's body: no headset tracks a torso, so the body frame is derived from the head — its origin is the head's position, its orientation the head's yaw with pitch and roll removed, and that yaw re-seats lazily (after the head has turned past a threshold for a delay, at a rate, stopping within a band) rather than every frame; a body-framed surface therefore stays put while the wearer looks around and comes along when they turn. Hand-framed surfaces follow a tracked hand or its held controller; world-framed surfaces hold a pose in the local reference space; docked-framed surfaces are presented on the docked output's plane (and only exist while docked).

entry.name: body
entry.summary: follows the body, not the head

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the manager. Existing anchoring objects are not affected.

request.name: get_anchoring

description.summary: extend a layer surface with spatial anchoring

request.description:
Create an anchoring object for the given layer surface. A layer surface may be extended at most once; a second request raises the already_anchored error.
Anchoring state lives and dies with the layer surface role: when the layer surface is destroyed, the anchoring object becomes inert. Any requests on an inert object will be ignored except the destroy request; there won't be any more events referencing it.

event.name: frames
event.description: The set of frames surfaces can currently anchor to, as a bitfield whose bit number frame is set for each available frame (bit 0 is head, bit 4 is world). Sent on bind and whenever the set changes (a hand losing tracking, the dock connecting). Requesting an absent frame is not an error: the surface is presented in its fallback frame (see zxr_anchored_layer_v1.set_frame) until the requested frame becomes available.

interface.name: zxr_anchored_layer_v1

description.summary: spatial anchoring state of a layer surface

interface.description:
Spatial anchoring state for one layer surface. All state set through this interface is double-buffered; it is applied on the next wl_surface.commit of the layer surface, atomically with the layer-shell state committed there.
If a client never sets a frame, the compositor presents the surface in the body frame — floating in front of the user, following them when they turn, free of their head's motion — with a compositor-chosen angular size; layer-shell clients unaware of this protocol therefore remain usable unmodified, and nothing is head-locked unless it asks to be.

entry.name: invalid_exclusive_angle
entry.summary: exclusive angle negative or not smaller than the frame extent

entry.name: invalid_pose
entry.summary: pose set for a frame other than world, or not a rigid transform

request.name: destroy
request.description: Remove the spatial anchoring. The layer surface falls back to the compositor's default presentation for its layer, as if the anchoring object had never existed.

request.name: set_frame
request.description: Set the reference frame the surface's layer-shell anchor edges are interpreted in. If the frame is currently unavailable (see zxr_layer_anchoring_v1.frames), the compositor presents the surface in that frame's fallback until it becomes available: hand frames fall back to the body frame, the docked frame to the head frame. Values set in this way are double-buffered, see wl_surface.commit.

request.name: set_pose
request.description: Set the transform from the surface's local space to the local reference space, for surfaces in the world frame: a rigid transform as 16 IEEE 754 binary32 values, column-major, native endianness. Setting a pose while the pending frame is not world raises the invalid_pose error, as does a non-rigid matrix. Values set in this way are double-buffered, see wl_surface.commit.

request.name: set_angular_size
request.description: Set the horizontal angle the surface subtends, in degrees; the vertical angle follows from the surface's aspect ratio, and the presentation distance from the frame's canonical distance. The size must be greater than zero and at most 180, otherwise the invalid_angular_size error is raised. If never set, the compositor chooses a size appropriate to the surface's layer. Values set in this way are double-buffered, see wl_surface.commit.

request.name: set_exclusive_angle

description.summary: reserve an angular band at the anchor

request.description: Reserve an angular band along the surface's layer-shell anchor edges, in degrees measured from the frame rectangle's edge inward, that the compositor keeps free of other exclusive-zone-respecting content in the same frame — the spatial analog of zwlr_layer_surface_v1.set_exclusive_zone. A value of zero, the default, reserves nothing. A negative value or a value not smaller than the frame's extent on that axis raises the invalid_exclusive_angle error. Values set in this way are double-buffered, see wl_surface.commit.

event.name: frame_extent
event.description: The angular rectangle of the surface's current frame: the extents within which anchor edges and exclusive angles are resolved. Sent after the frame first applies and whenever the extents change (including on fallback, when they are the fallback frame's).
